hook.convey: one whole shared into EQUAL parts → each part gets a name from how many equal parts the whole has: 4 equal parts → 1/4; a roti shared at home, a paper strip folded for a drawing

use.hi: Ghar mein ek roti 4 bachchon mein barabar baantni hai. Har bachche ke hisse ka ek pakka naam hota hai.
use.en: At home a roti is to be shared equally among 4 children. Each child's part has a proper name.

use.hi: Drawing ke liye kaagaz ki patti barabar hisson mein modte hain. Roti ki tarah, har hisse ka naam hota hai.
use.en: For a drawing we fold a paper strip into equal parts. As with a roti, each part has a name.

explain.convey: roti in 4 equal parts → one part = 1/4 = one of 4 equal parts = a fractional unit; the bottom number = how many equal parts the whole has; the card: a same-size roti in 8 equal parts on its own board → the child names its unit

viewCaption.hi: Yahan wahi roti ek seedhi patti ki tarah khuli hai: 4 barabar hisse, aur ek hisse mein rang.
viewCaption.en: Here the same roti is opened out like a straight strip: 4 equal parts, and one part coloured.

point.hi: Yeh roti 4 barabar hisson mein bati hai. Rang wala ek hissa poori roti ka 1/4 hai, ek-chauthaai. Poore ke barabar hisson mein se aisa ek hissa fractional unit kehlata hai.
point.en: This roti is in 4 equal parts. The one coloured part is 1/4 of the whole roti, one quarter. One such part out of a whole's equal parts is called a fractional unit.

pointAlt.hi: Socho chaar dost yeh roti barabar baant-te hain. Har dost ke haath chaar barabar hisson mein se ek aata hai, jaise yeh rang wala hissa: roti ka 1/4. Aise ek hisse ko fractional unit kehte hain.
pointAlt.en: Picture four friends sharing this roti equally. Each friend gets one of the four equal parts, like this coloured part: 1/4 of the roti. One part like that is called a fractional unit.

prompt.hi: Ab bagal wali roti dekho, utni hi badi, par 8 barabar hisson mein bati. Uska ek hissa kaunsa fractional unit hai?
